note: Verified against legislation.tas.gov.au on 2026-08-26. The Supreme Court Rules 2000 carry their own time code in Part 4: r 47 (a period of days not expressed as clear days excludes the first day and includes the last), r 48 (the period between 23 December and 7 January is not reckoned for filing, amendment or delivery of a pleading or appearance), r 50 (periods of less than 6 days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and Court holidays) and r 51 (a period expiring on a Saturday, Sunday or Court holiday runs to the next day that is none of those). 'Court holiday' is defined by r 19 and is not the same as a public holiday; the script approximates Court holidays and registry closures with the weekend-and-public-holiday table (Hobart basis, Easter Tuesday included), and every computed date carries a warning to confirm the registry was open. Acts Interpretation Act 1931 s 29 could not be retrieved from the publisher on the checked date (the site returned 404 or 'Internal Error' for every candidate identifier) and is recorded as pending-verification; no period rule depends on it because Part 4 is self-contained. Magistrates Court (Civil Division) Rules 1998 periods are not tabled here. An entry returned to pending-verification fails closed until re-verified.

computation_provisions.summary: Computation of a number of days: a period of a particular number of days, not expressed to be clear days, excludes the first day and includes the last day (r 47). A period of less than 6 days appointed or allowed for doing any act does not include a Saturday, Sunday or Court holiday (r 50). If the period for doing any act expires on a Saturday, Sunday or Court holiday, the act may be done on the next day which is not a Saturday, Sunday or Court holiday (r 51). Court holidays are New Year's Day; Good Friday, Easter Monday and Easter Tuesday; Christmas Day and the 3 days following; and any other day appointed by the Chief Justice (r 19); each registry is open every day except Saturdays, Sundays and Court holidays (r 20(1)). Extension and abridgment sit in r 52.

computation_provisions.summary: Unless the Court or a judge otherwise directs, the period between the twenty-third day of December and the seventh day of January following is not to be reckoned in the computation of the times appointed or allowed by the rules for the filing, amendment or delivery of any pleading or appearance (r 48, as substituted by S.R. 2016 No 122 from 11 January 2017). Applies only to appearances and pleadings — not to notices of appeal.

period_rules.label: Notice of appearance after service of writ within Tasmania
period_rules.trigger: Service of the writ (or other originating process requiring an appearance) on the defendant within the jurisdiction of the Court
warnings: The 7-day period is the period 'limited by a writ' for service within the jurisdiction; the writ itself states the time — check the writ. Service elsewhere in Australia gives 21 days (r 99(a)); service outside Australia gives 42 days from service unless the Court otherwise orders (rr 99(b), 147E).
A defendant may file a notice of appearance at any time before judgment or final order (r 164(1)), subject to default-judgment consequences under Part 11.

Under r 48 the days from 24 December to 6 January are not counted for filing an appearance (unless the Court or a judge otherwise directs); the encoded range takes the narrower reading of 'between' — an inclusive reading would also skip 23 December and 7 January.

Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed Tasmanian holiday (Hobart basis, Easter Tuesday included); r 51 turns on Court holidays as defined by r 19, which may differ from public holidays and may include days appointed by the Chief Justice — confirm the registry was open on the candidate date.

evidence.method: Plain HTTP fetch of the official current in-force reprint; period and trigger in r 98 confirmed exactly, with rr 99, 147E and 164 read for the warnings.

period_rules.label: Defence to statement of claim
period_rules.trigger: The later of (a) delivery of the statement of claim and (b) the expiry of the time limited for filing a notice of appearance — supply that later date as the trigger date
warnings: The 21 days apply unless the plaintiff has applied for judgment under Division 3 of Part 11 (summary judgment); if such an application is dismissed or leave to defend is granted, the defence is due 8 days after the order or within the period the order fixes (r 266(2)), and where a statement of claim is filed in default under r 353(2) the defence may be filed within 8 days after its filing (r 266(3)) — none of those limbs is computed here.
The trigger is a 'later of' test: this entry computes from whichever date the user supplies as the later event and does not itself compare the two limbs.

Under r 48 the days from 24 December to 6 January are not counted for filing or delivering a pleading (unless the Court or a judge otherwise directs); the encoded range takes the narrower reading of 'between' — an inclusive reading would also skip 23 December and 7 January.

Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed Tasmanian holiday (Hobart basis, Easter Tuesday included); r 51 turns on Court holidays as defined by r 19, which may differ from public holidays and may include days appointed by the Chief Justice — confirm the registry was open on the candidate date.

evidence.method: Plain HTTP fetch of the official current in-force reprint; period and both limbs of the trigger in r 266(1) confirmed exactly, r 266(2)-(3) read for the warnings.
evidence.version: Authorised reprint published 29 July 2026 (publisher PublicationDate 20260729), accessed 26 August 2026

period_rules.label: Notice of appeal to the Full Court from a final judgment
period_rules.trigger: The date on which the final judgment was pronounced (or, for the refusal of an application, the date of the refusal)
warnings: The 21 days apply only to an appeal from a final judgment; an appeal that is not from a final judgment must be instituted within 10 days (r 659) and is not computed by this entry. 'Final judgment' and 'interlocutory judgment' are defined for leave purposes in r 680A — confirm the characterisation before relying on the 21-day period.

An appeal is instituted by filing the original notice of appeal in the Principal Registry and serving a copy on each party directly affected (r 660); the notice is given for an ordinary sitting of the Full Court on a date fixed by the Principal Registrar (r 657(5)).
The r 48 vacation exclusion applies to pleadings and appearances only and is not applied to this period; the general extension power in r 52 remains available.

The Principal Registry is at Hobart, so the holiday table is Hobart-based; rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed Tasmanian holiday, but r 51 turns on Court holidays as defined by r 19 — confirm the registry was open on the candidate date.
